feed.title: deja-vu docs
feed.subtitle: Pages of the deja-vu documentation that changed, newest first.

entry.title: Delete Kiro session history — deja-vu
entry.summary: Kiro keeps CLI and IDE sessions in two different trees under ~/.kiro/sessions. Where each one is, how to remove one session or all, and what else Kiro keeps.

entry.title: Find the coding session where you solved it — deja-vu
entry.summary: How to search chat history across every coding agent on the machine, by the token you remember rather than the topic you half-remember.

entry.title: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and 32 more agents — deja-vu
entry.summary: The thirty-five coding agents deja indexes today, where each stores its history, and how to add a new one.

entry.title: Claude Code lost your context: how to get it back — deja-vu
entry.summary: A crash, a cleared window or a restart takes the agent's context but not the transcript — how to get the work back and stop paying for it next time.

entry.title: Add memory to aider: its read-only context — deja-vu
entry.summary: aider appends every message to one markdown log and reads none of it back. deja keeps a read-only context file current and indexes every agent on the machine.

entry.title: Cherry Studio memory: every agent's sessions — deja-vu
entry.summary: Cherry Studio writes its agent sessions under its own app data. deja reads them, and hands the same memory to every other agent on the machine.

entry.title: Add memory to Claude Code: every agent's sessions — deja-vu
entry.summary: How to give Claude Code recall over every coding agent's sessions on this machine — the MCP server, the SessionStart hook and the plugin marketplace.

entry.title: Add memory to Command Code: past sessions — deja-vu
entry.summary: Command Code logs a session per project and starts each one cold. deja wires its MCP server, hooks, skill and command, and indexes every agent here.

entry.title: Add memory to Gemini CLI: every agent's sessions — deja-vu
entry.summary: How to give Gemini CLI recall over every coding agent's sessions on this machine — one extension install, and what the CLI install adds on top.

entry.title: Add memory to Kiro: every agent's sessions — deja-vu
entry.summary: Kiro keeps every session on disk — the CLI one way, the IDE another — and starts each new one empty. deja reads both stores and answers from them in any agent.

entry.title: Add memory to Qwen Code: every agent's sessions — deja-vu
entry.summary: How to give Qwen Code recall over every coding agent's sessions on this machine — the Gemini extension format, and Claude-format marketplaces.

entry.title: Add memory to Roo Code: every agent's sessions — deja-vu
entry.summary: Roo Code has no lifecycle hooks yet, so deja arrives as an MCP server, a skill that says when to call it, a /deja command and an approval entry.

entry.title: Add memory to ZCode: recall past sessions — deja-vu
entry.summary: ZCode keeps a project log and a CLI database, and reads neither back. deja wires its MCP server and two hooks in one config file, and indexes every agent.

entry.title: Resume yesterday's Claude Code or Codex session — deja-vu
entry.summary: Find the session across every agent on the machine, then reopen it in the tool that owns it — or take the digest instead of the whole conversation.

entry.title: Search your Claude Code and Codex history — deja-vu
entry.summary: deja search syntax: exact and phrase queries, natural language with stop words, fuzzy typo tolerance, confidence tiers, and optional local semantic recall.

entry.summary: Where Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, opencode and thirty-one more coding agents keep their conversation history on disk, what is inside those files, and how each format drifts.
